json.title: Northvale grid queue reaches 4.8 GW of data center requests, 0.9 GW signed
json.summary:
Data center developers have asked the Northvale Grid Authority to connect 4.8 GW of new load, compared with 1.9 GW a year before, according to the operator's quarterly interconnection queue report published on 12 November 2026. The queue holds 31 data center requests.

Only 0.9 GW of that total has signed interconnection agreements. Another 1.4 GW has finished system impact studies, while 2.5 GW has yet to be studied. Studies now average 14 months, up from 8 months in 2024.

The authority said its transmission system can take about 1.1 GW of extra load before 2029 without new substations or line upgrades, and it put the cost of the upgrades needed for the queued requests at $2.3 billion, charged to the customers that need them.
json.why_it_matters: The report separates contracted load from requested load, and the difference is large: most of the queue has no agreement and more than half has not been studied. For buyers and lenders, a connection date in Northvale now depends on contract position and on upgrade costs that the report has not yet allocated among projects.
json.expert_lens: The 1.1 GW of headroom before 2029 sits close to the 0.9 GW already under agreement, which suggests little unupgraded capacity is left for later requests. A readiness deposit of $50,000 per megawatt from 1 March 2027 will likely thin out speculative filings, but it does not shorten the 14-month study time for projects already waiting. The two campuses behind 1.6 GW of requests have no signed agreements and are seeking project financing, so their lenders face a connection with no published date. The next signal to watch is the queue report due in February 2027, and whether the signed share moves above 0.9 GW.
